sources.quote: an enclosure at least 1.2 metres high that a 10 centimetre ball cannot pass under and that is not easy to climb
sources.title: Sécurisez votre piscine extérieure pour prévenir tout risque de noyade | Gouvernement du Québec
sources.evidence: An enclosure around a pool must have a height of at least 1.2 m and prevent the passage of a spherical object of 10 cm in diameter (between bars, between the base of the fence and the ground), and be free of fixing elements, projections or perforated parts that could facilitate climbing.

sources.quote: owners of those older pools have been given until 30 September 2027 to comply
sources.title: Piscines résidentielles - La ministre des Affaires municipales respecte son engagement de repousser la date butoir du Règlement sur la sécurité des piscines résidentielles
sources.evidence: Owners of pools installed before November 1, 2010 have been given an additional 2-year delay and now have until September 30, 2027 to ensure their installations comply with the Regulation on the safety of residential pools. Pools built before November 1, 2010 previously had acquired rights and were not subject to protective measures.

sources.quote: Ontario Regulation 565 under the Health Protection and Promotion Act, covering water chemistry and operator training
sources.title: R.R.O. 1990, Reg. 565: PUBLIC POOLS | ontario.ca
sources.evidence: O. Reg. 565: Public Pools under the Health Protection and Promotion Act sets out requirements and standards for operations, maintenance, and equipment at public pools and public spas. Every owner of a public pool or public spa must designate an operator overseeing the safe operation of the facility; the regulation includes requirements for water chemistry, facilities, equipment, signage and staffing.

sources.quote: with penalties reaching up to CAD 10 million for a corporation
sources.title: Frequently Asked Questions about Canada's Anti-Spam Legislation | CRTC
sources.evidence: The maximum amount of an administrative monetary penalty (AMP), per violation, for an individual is $1 million, and for a business it is $10 million.

sources.quote: implied consent from a purchase generally expires two years after the sale
sources.title: From Canada’s Anti-Spam Legislation (CASL) Guidance on Implied Consent | CRTC
sources.evidence: You may have an existing business relationship if the recipient has made a purchase or lease of goods, services, land or interest in land within the two-year period immediately before the day on which the message was sent. Implied consent is typically a period of 2 years after the event that starts the relationship (e.g. purchase of a good).

sources.quote: carrying a cooling off right commonly of 10 days plus prescribed terms on delivery dates and total cost
sources.title: Your rights when signing or cancelling a contract | ontario.ca
sources.evidence: You have a cooling-off period when you sign contracts for a product or service you buy from a door-to-door salesperson (also called a direct agreement). You have the right to cancel a contract without any reason within a 10-day cooling-off period, beginning the day you receive a written copy of the agreement.

sources.quote: was and now pricing on covers follows the ordinary selling price rules
sources.title: Ordinary selling price - Competition Bureau Canada
sources.evidence: When promoting a sale, the regular price must be a price the item is genuinely sold at, and businesses must be able to prove it. To prove that a regular price is valid, it must meet one of two legal tests: Volume test (more than 50% of sales of the product were at that price or higher within a reasonable period) or Time test (the product was offered for sale, in good faith, at that price or higher for a substantial period of time).
